frames.review_note: Minor only. Nagoji's collar ring sits at the front, not the side, and a short length of chain hangs from it down his chest. This is not above anyone's head, so it does not break the rule against vertical chains. A hanging lantern lights the hold warmly, so it is dim rather than near darkness. The pale slits overhead read as gaps in the deck seams, not open sky, which fits 1.3. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists under the manacles, wrist chain, ankle cuffs with hobble chain, barefoot. His right hand lies flat on the planks. A ragged ochre flap covers his left forearm, so no brand shows. The image is tilted hard and upright boards split the pens. Pen chains run collar to collar and rise to the beams at a slant. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Hands and feet are sound. The dark, plain ceiling at top right easily holds both captions, and the dark foreground planks at bottom left are a second option. v01 to v04 were not offered as candidates in this round (they show open sky and storm through the hull).

Minor only. Nagoji's collar ring hangs at the front, not the side. His tunic drapes as ragged sleeve cloth over both arms, which reads a little sleeved but keeps the left forearm covered as required. His eyes are fully closed, not half closed. The pen chain runs fairly taut at chest height between the collars instead of drooping onto the plank. The faces, irons, closed hold with lantern glow, Nagoji left and Keshavrao right, and Keshavrao's lock (young, faint moustache, ragged short hair, grey-brown tunic, no stud, thin unbandaged hands) all match. The upper-right wall suits the balloon and the bottom strip over the knees suits the caption. v02 is the same art with no pen chain and a bare left forearm. v01 is rejected: it is set on an open deck in rain with red-waistcoated guards.

Minor only. The boot shadows are cast straight onto the underside of the solid deck planks, which is physically loose but clearly reads as the scripted beat of running feet crossing overhead. The frame has no text, no noose (the ropes are coils and lashings), no open sky and no painted balloons. Grey-white light cuts through the seams and water drips down onto the beam. The low-detail dark planking along the top band (roughly y 0 to 0.2, left and right) takes both jagged balloons without covering the shadows. Tails go to the top edge because the sailors are off panel above.

Minor. The guard's raised hand grips the edge of the canvas awning, not the hatch frame. Besides the cross-belt he wears a narrow waist belt (not wide, and no key ring). Faint plank highlights at the far left (about x 0.01 to 0.07, y 0.49 to 0.54) could suggest stencil marks at a squint, but a contrast check shows wood grain, not letterforms. The guard look matches: lean, dark-bearded, steel morion, soaked buff jerkin with cross-belt over a shirt, flintlock in hand, rain pouring through the hatch as the awning is dragged across. v01 is preferred: its small top-left box sits on dark beams clear of the musket hand, while v02's tall left box reaches down to the hand gripping the musket.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor only. The ladder is not in frame; the musket lies by the right-hand post, so 'near the foot of the ladder' is implied rather than shown (2.4 shows the ladder). The background prisoners look toward the camera and foreground rather than plainly at the musket, but Nagoji and Keshavrao both look down-right at it. The irons match 1.2: collar-to-collar pen chain through side rings, bandaged wrists under manacles, hobble chains. Nagoji's left forearm is covered by bandage and an ochre flap. Captions go in the top band: beams above the heads, with the right half fully clear. Rejected: v02 (no collars), v03 (no musket), v06 (a deck scene in daylight with a guard). v05, v07 and v08 have Nagoji gazing up and away from the musket. v04 has Keshavrao's second wrist apparently unmanacled and oversized dangling chains. Backup v01 stages the beat best (ladder, beam, every head turned) but has no collar-to-collar pen chain, so it matches 1.2 and 2.3 less well.

Clean. The guard is seen from behind in a morion and buff jerkin with cross-belt, silhouetted in the open hatch against rain and storm light, head turned toward the deck, never looking down. The painted balloons have long tails, but both point at the guard (the correct speaker), and the drawn balloons will cover them. The frame is 2.65:1 and the slot is about 3.97:1, so set visible_rect to roughly [0,0,2043,515] to keep the hatch, guard and beams without letterboxing. v05 is the same art pre-letterboxed to a 5.35:1 strip, which the contain fit would place thinner than the slot. v02 is an outdoor fort scene (reject). v03 and v04 are acceptable but have oversized painted balloons.

Framing is a medium-wide two-shot rather than a 'close' one, which suits the 2.53:1 strip. Keshavrao's eyes are downcast toward the floor, slightly screen-left, rather than clearly toward the musket (screen-right in 2.1). The seawater reads as a wet sheen on the boards rather than a visible threading current. Identity and irons are correct: Nagoji on the left with clean chin, curled moustache, stud, bandaged wrists and left forearm covered; Keshavrao on the right; pen chain collar to collar. Nagoji looks up at the lit hatch stairwell, where rain comes down as in 1.5. v01, v03 and v04 drop Nagoji's wrist bandages, run a chain from collar to wrists, and are 1.5:1, needing a heavy crop. v02 puts an armed guard in the hold (reject).

Minor. The floor carries a shallow sheet of water, and water cascades down the ladder steps, rather than a single thin thread (it matches the 2.3 stairwell). The current does curl around the stock. The flintlock (cock and frizzen visible) lies against the beam, and the ladder rises into grey storm light. The visible strip (y 187-575) is exactly the 5.09:1 slot, with a clear caption band over the dark beams at upper left. v04 is the same art full-frame; it needs a crop to about [0,245,1959,630] and would lose most of the sky. v01 is also acceptable, but its current runs by the barrel rather than the stock, and it needs a heavy crop. v02 is an unrelated scene (reject).

Acceptable, with minor issues. The wide, distant view shows the broadside surge: water rushes down the aisle into the pens and the collar-to-collar pen chains snap sideways along the rows, never upward. There is no text, noose, blood or anachronism (glass lanterns are fine on a Portuguese ship). Minor points: the rendering is more photographic and cinematic than the inked neighbouring panels; the extras are bare-chested in loincloths rather than grey and brown rags; the tilt is modest and the 'almost weightless' moment is not really shown, since the men are bracing, which reads a little like galley rowers. The caption fits cleanly in the large dark ceiling area at top left (x 0.02 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.2).

Acceptable. This is a clean edit of the previously accepted v03 with the painted balloons removed and no artefacts left behind. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, torn ochre tunic with a ragged flap covering his left forearm, bandaged wrists, hinged collar. He shouts down the line while the men beside him copy the overhead grip. Deviations: he grips the beam with his hands apart instead of hooking both forearms over it with his wrists together, and his collar chain hangs down the front from the centre of the collar instead of drooping to one side from a side ring. The blue-lit grating at upper right reads as storm light through a hatch grating, not open sky. There is room for lettering over the low-detail beams at top left (x 0.0 to 0.3, y 0.0 to 0.18) and top right (x 0.6 to 0.98, y 0.0 to 0.2), clear of the raised hands.

Minor only. A thin black frame border and white margin are painted inside the image (crop them at placement). Nagoji's wrist chain runs longer than a forearm and meets his collar chain near Keshavrao's cuff. There is a small pale window-like patch at the extreme top-left edge. Otherwise sound: the lantern-lit hold matches pages 2 and 3. Nagoji is on the left (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, ochre rags) and clamps his bandaged hand on Keshavrao's forearm, with the inner forearm turned from camera. Keshavrao is on the right (ragged short hair, faint moustache, grey-brown rags, collar with the side pen chain, bare hands), sliding away and reaching for a barrel. The chain meets his cuff. There is no text, and the panel is silent as the script calls for. Rejected: v02 and v03 show Keshavrao with no iron collar, and v03 also has a bright storm window. v04 puts Nagoji in a white tunic with a red sash. v01 is on the open deck with guards and sky.

Acceptable. This is a tight two-shot with Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, faces close and water streaming down them. Nagoji is on-model: curled moustache, light captivity stubble only, gold stud, ochre rags, bandaged wrists, collar. Keshavrao matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, collar, no ear stud. The collar-to-collar chain droops between them. Nagoji's left forearm shows at the bottom from the outer side with a bandaged wrist and no brand, which is acceptable. Lettering room is limited to the dark top band (x 0.0 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.16) and the dark left edge (x 0.0 to 0.18, y 0.16 to 0.45). The two long lines may need balloons that just touch the top of Nagoji's hair, but no face would be covered.

Acceptable. Keshavrao is alone and on-model: short ragged hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown torn tunic, hinged collar with a side ring, no ear stud. His eyes are wide in the gloom, and lightning glows through the seams overhead. Minor points: the lightning does not really light half his face, which is lit evenly and warmly; the render is darker and more photographic than 3.4; his eyes glance screen-right, although Nagoji is off-panel to the left (placed by 3.4 and by the collar chain leaving the frame at left). The large, plain, dark plank wall on the left (x 0.02 to 0.5, y 0.02 to 0.6) holds all three balloons easily. The tail for Nagoji's off-panel line points to the left edge.

Minor only. The over-the-shoulder framing works: Keshavrao is seen from behind (short hair, grey-brown tunic, collar) and Nagoji matches his sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, collar, bandaged fists, ankle cuffs with a hobble chain), with his fist round the drooping chain. His left arm is wrapped in a ragged ochre sleeve rather than the sleeveless tunic, which still keeps the brand hidden. The forearm-long chain between his wrists is not clearly shown. The plank bowing inward behind him is not distinct. Water sheets down the walls, which is heavier than the scripted spray but reads as seepage through the hull, not rain. There is no painted text or balloons. For lettering, use the low-detail wall at upper right (about x 0.68 to 0.98, y 0.03 to 0.40) and the upper centre (x 0.30 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.17), away from Nagoji's face.

Keshavrao matches his sheet: short ragged wet hair, faint moustache, softer young face, grey-brown tunic, iron collar. The ghost of a smile is there, and there is no text. There is a painted white margin with a thin black frame line about 20 px in on every edge. Trim about 22 px from each side before placing it, or the panel gets a double border (tail and face fractions above refer to the untrimmed image). The background planks are warm, bright and softly blurred, with a slight mosaic upscale texture. That is lighter than the dark, cold-lit hold in 4.1, but acceptable for a tight close-up. For lettering, use the plain wall at upper right (x 0.62 to 0.97, y 0.04 to 0.45).

This is the closed hold, wide, with lightning lines through the deck seams and chained men clinging to beams and each other, mouths open and eye-whites showing. There is no text and no painted boxes. Minor points: the light comes through plank seams rather than specifically round a hatch cover, and it reads as a dim blue flicker more than one harsh white freeze-frame. The third man from the left has a faint reddish flush on his forehead. It is diffuse, with no gash or drip, so it does not read as gore at print size. The second man (curly hair, moustache) has stubble and no ear stud, so he should not be mistaken for Nagoji. Put the caption in the dark ceiling planks along the top (x 0.30 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.12).

v02 is acceptable. The camera looks straight up at the underside of the deck at the moment of impact. The planks bow downward, and sheets of water and grit pour through the seams while the beams and hull timbers stay whole. There are no figures, no text, no sky and no open hatch. The painted blank balloons sit upper left (before the impact) and lower right (after it), with no tails. That is right, because both speakers are sailors off panel above the deck. Both balloons bleed off the frame edges, but the letterer covers them. v01 is rejected: its painted balloon tails point at men in the hold instead of off-panel sailors, the ceiling shows bright openings, and it adds figures the script does not call for.

Nagoji is on the left and matches his sheet: moustache, gold ear stud, clean chin with light captivity stubble, collar, bandaged wrists, manacles with a short chain, no brand visible. Keshavrao is on the right and matches his: short hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, collar. They are waist-deep, with chains dragging in the surge and a bearded prisoner gasping behind them. The ring bolted in the beam at upper right is clear, with the chain running to it. Hands are sound and there is no text. Minor points: Keshavrao shouts with his chin up but is not tight at Nagoji's ear (the prisoner sits between them), and he looks up-left rather than toward the ring. The background prisoner wears a small gold ear stud, though his full beard keeps him distinct from Nagoji. The warm golden light is warmer than the cool blue of 4.1. For lettering, use the ceiling beams across the top (the PRISONER balloon about x 0.35 to 0.55, y 0.03 to 0.20; the KESHAVRAO balloon about x 0.56 to 0.82, y 0.02 to 0.20), keeping the ring at about x 0.90, y 0.10 clear.

v02 is acceptable. It shows the ring bolted under the overhead beam, cracks and lifting splinters around the plate, and the chain rising at a slant from out of frame lower left, inside a lantern-lit hold that matches 4.5 and 5.2. Minor points: the plate uses crisp hexagonal nuts that look slightly machine-made, the chain is heavier than the collar chain in neighbouring panels, and the hold looks dry here. The painted box upper left sits over plain beam and gets covered. v01 is rejected because it is set outdoors in daylight with palm trees and a stockade fence, so it is not the closed hold.

v06 is acceptable. The ring hangs from one bolt in a freshly splintered beam, and its chain drops slack into the water at the far end of the row. The row of collared, manacled prisoners is dragged sideways and leans to the left. Nagoji (front left) matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, bandaged hands, hinged collar. Keshavrao (second) matches his. Water pours through the deck seams, and the hull timbers stay whole, as 4.4 requires. The caption box upper left covers only ceiling. The backup v04 is weaker because the ring chain runs taut at a diagonal instead of sagging into the water. v05 is rejected because the hull is smashed open to the sea and rain at right, which breaks 4.4. v03 is rejected because the ring hangs detached from the chain, which anticipates 5.5. v02 is rejected because the lead prisoner is a bearded curly-haired man who reads as a bearded Nagoji, and nobody wears collars. v01 is rejected because it is set outside the ship on open sea with guards on deck.

Clean pick. v06 is v05 (the version already accepted) with the painted balloon removed, and the repainted ceiling, beams and barrels in the upper right show no leftover marks. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 3 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble, gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, short-chained manacles, hinged collar with a side ring. The tunic flap covers his left forearm down to the bandage, so the brand stays hidden. He rounds on the prisoners with teeth bared while they cry out with raised fists and reaching hands. The waist-deep flooded hold, warm light, barrels and dripping seams match 5.2 and 5.4. There is no text, noose, blood or anachronism, and all hands are sound. Two minor points: a small grated opening at the top left shows rain outside, which reads as a hull scuttle rather than open sky; and the left-hand pen chain disappears behind Nagoji's hip. Neither needs a regeneration. Put the single NAGOJI balloon over the low-detail beams and barrels up and to the right of his head, at about x 0.62 to 0.82 and y 0.03 to 0.30. It covers no face and no hand.

v04 is acceptable. Nagoji (left) and Keshavrao (right) grip the chain in manacled fists and haul it level toward the camera, feet braced in the flood water. The ring hangs from the beam by a single bolt, and its chain drops behind them without attaching to either collar, so nothing pulls on a neck. Nagoji has the moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud and bandaged wrists. Keshavrao has short hacked hair, a faint moustache and no stud. Both painted balloons sit at upper left over background with tails toward Nagoji, the correct speaker. Minor point: the beam around the ring is not visibly splintered as it was in 5.2. The backup v05 is almost identical, with the second painted balloon over the upper-right background. v06, v07, v08 and v09 are rejected because the ring chain runs down in a V into the collar chain between the two men, so it reads as hanging from their necks. v09 also has a long painted tail across the art. v02 and v03 are rejected because the floor is dry and the ring is bolted to the deck in the foreground, not in the beam. v01 is rejected because it is outdoors in daylight with guards.

v03 is acceptable. The freed chain whips away through a splash in the water between the two men, who stagger apart and look up into the open space overhead. Each still wears an empty hinged collar and wrist cuffs, and the ankle hobble chains are visible above the shallow water. Nagoji matches his sheet (moustache, clean chin, small ear stud, bandaged hands), and his left forearm is covered by the ochre sleeve, so the brand stays hidden. Keshavrao matches his sheet, with no stud. The wide frame suits the full-width row, and the lantern-lit hold matches 5.4. Minor points: Nagoji's wrist chain shows as short lengths hanging from each cuff, the tearing-out of the bolt is not shown, and Keshavrao has a bandage on one hand. The backup v04 (v05 is almost identical) shows deeper water that hides the hobbles, and the chain lies still instead of whipping. v02 works but is a 3:2 frame that would crop badly into a full-width row. v01 is rejected because its four painted boxes would stay blank in a panel with no text, the water is only a shallow puddle, and the empty rings are still bolted to the post.

Minor issues only. The 'its men stare after them' beat is implied rather than staged, because the background prisoners are still bent over their own rings. Nagoji's collar ring sits at the front rather than the side. Everything else matches: both men wear empty collars, manacles and hobbles; Nagoji has his ear stud and a clean chin, and his left forearm is wrapped; the hold is flooded and lantern-lit. There is clear space for balloons over the top-left background and for captions over the water. The v04 and v05 frames are pixel-identical. v01 and v02 were rejected: the floor is dry and no other prisoners are present. v06 was not chosen: its long painted tails cut across Nagoji's head.

Minor only. The musket floats half-submerged at the surface in the near foreground instead of lying on the floor under the water. Keshavrao's moustache is a little fuller than 'faint'. A short loose chain hangs from Nagoji's right manacle into the water. Otherwise clean. Nagoji is on the left looking up at the lit hatch, with thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, empty collar with side ring and his left forearm covered by a tunic flap and bandage. Keshavrao is on the right looking at him. Both stand about thigh-deep. The dark ceiling beams across the top (x 0.45 to 0.92, y 0.0 to 0.2) take balloons 0 and 1, and the open water at the bottom centre (x 0.35 to 0.8, y 0.8 to 0.97) takes balloon 2.

Acceptable with a small setting quibble: behind the water is a wooden plank rim that reads a little like a trough edge, and his dhoti looks dry above the waterline, although 6.2 has him thigh-deep. In a tight insert with the bottom caption over most of the water, this reads well enough. v03 shows the lock best: the frizzen stands open above a dry, empty pan. The bandaged, manacled hands grip soundly and the forearms are covered or out of frame. v01 was rejected: Nagoji crouches dry beside a tub with his feet out of the water, contradicting the flooded hold, and his left forearm is bare and exposed.

Acceptable, with continuity notes. The camera looks up the ladder from a low angle. Nagoji climbs with both manacled, bandaged hands on the rungs and the musket pinned under his near arm, and the hobble chain is visible between his ankle cuffs. He looks back down with moustache, clean chin and gold stud intact, and the brand arm is wrapped. Keshavrao is seen from behind at the foot of the ladder, collar and manacle on, in the water. Notes: (1) Nagoji's iron collar is not visible. His hunched shoulder and long hair hide his neck, so it reads as hidden rather than removed, but it is a soft continuity gap against 6.2. (2) This ladder is round poles lashed with rope, where the ladders in 6.2 and 6.5 are plain wood. (3) A glass lantern and open-flame lamps burn in the hold, which 6.2 does not show. This is allowed in a Portuguese setting but is a small lighting change. Lettering: the Nagoji balloon goes in the dark ceiling at the upper left (x 0.18 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.15), with its tail to his mouth. The caption goes in the dark ceiling beams at the upper right (x 0.66 to 0.97, y 0.02 to 0.2).

Clean. This is Nagoji's point of view straight up the ladder. The guard is a black silhouette on the top rungs, backlit by lightning and rain in the open hatch. The upturned brim and crest of his morion read clearly. One hand grips the ladder rail and the other points the musket barrel down at the camera. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Minor: a dark twisted rope or post shows behind the lower rungs, and this ladder has no rope lashings, unlike 6.4. The GUARD balloon goes on the dark wood planks at the upper right (x 0.72 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.26), with a short tail to the silhouette's mouth under the helmet brim.

Acceptable with minor deviations. The beat reads clearly. The guard is thrown backward off balance, both hands off the ladder. Nagoji drives his reversed musket butt two-handed into the guard's open wrist without being gripped. His wrist chain swings between the cuffs, the guard's musket spins away into the dark at right, lightning shows in the open hatch and no injury is shown. The setting matches 6.5, 7.3 and 7.4: a flat-tread companion ladder whose foot vanishes into black flood water with no dry planks, a lamp-lit timber hold and rain falling through the hatch. The guard has a morion, buff jerkin, cream shirt and cross-belt, with no cuirass and nothing red. Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, long curly hair, empty iron collar, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti and bandaged manacled wrists. There is no text, blood or noose. Deviations: (1) This is a side-on medium-wide shot with full figures, not distant with small figures, though no injury is visible and at column width the figures print small. (2) Only his front foot is on a tread. The trailing foot is at the waterline, lifting out with a splash. (3) No hobble chain is drawn between the ankle cuffs, only short stubs. (4) The musket barrel is hidden behind his arm and torso, so only the stock shows. (5) The ear stud is tiny and reads dark rather than gold. (6) His far (left) forearm is bare between cuff and elbow, but no brand is drawn and the bandage and cuff cover the brand zone. Caption space: CAPTION 0 over the dark deck beams at top-left (x 0 to 0.35, y 0 to 0.28), clear of the lantern and figures. CAPTION 1 ('Bone cracked.') over the beams at top-right (x 0.78 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.14) or over the water at lower-right (x 0.7 to 1.0, y 0.88 to 1.0).

v07 is the only candidate and it is acceptable. It fixes the two main r4 geometry failures. The flat-tread ladder now rises straight into the single hatch, with the lightning and rain column directly at its top. The guard falls down the same shaft, seen through the gap between two treads, level with Nagoji's fists and within an arm's length of him, toward the black flood water at the ladder foot. That sets up 7.3, where the body floats at the foot of the ladder. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, hinged collar with its side ring, torn ochre sleeveless tunic and cream dhoti. His bandaged wrists sit in manacles joined by one short chain, and both fists grip the same tread. Both hands are sound. His cheek is pressed to the rail, eyes squeezed shut and face turned away from the fall, which is the script's 'does not look'. No brand shows, because the forearms are bandaged with their inner sides turned down. The guard is seen from above and behind, face hidden under his morion. He wears a buff jerkin with cross-belts, cream sleeves and a sword, and both arms are flung up. Each hand has five fingers. The hold matches 7.1 v12 and 7.3 v06: lamp-lit timber, lashed barrels, flooded floor and rain only down the hatch shaft. There is no text, blood, noose or anachronism. The panel is silent, so no lettering space is needed. Minor deviations: (1) The irons flaw from v06 is still there. Below the visible ankle cuff, whose hobble chain runs off behind the rail, a second metal ring wraps the heel of the same foot. It is small at print size and could be retouched. (2) The guard is lit, not the 'dark shape' half-silhouette the script asks for, though he still reads clearly as falling between the rungs. His breeches are a dark maroon, where 7.1 has dark brown. (3) Nagoji's treads sit on a second rail alongside the main ladder's right rail, so the ladder reads as a double-width companion. The structure is odd if studied, but it reads at a glance as Nagoji hugging the side of the same ladder. (4) The guard's pose is jackknifed at the hips, with his boots up near his raised hands. It is readable as a tumbling fall.

Clean and faithful to the r3 correction. The view is high, straight down the flat-tread companion ladder, with a brass lamp at left and lashed bales and barrels. The hold is flooded with no dry planks, and the lowest treads meet the water. The fallen guard floats face-down, half submerged, in a buff leather jerkin, cream shirt, dark breeches and boots. His face is hidden in the water and his morion floats beside him. The collared, manacled prisoners press back against the bales, waist-deep. There is no blood, text or noose, and the prisoners' hands are sound. The plain dark hull planking across the top-left (about x 0 to 0.42, y 0 to 0.12) is clear of every face for 'The ladder was clear.' Minor points only: the rendering is more photographic and less inked than 7.1 and 7.4 (the earlier 7.3 candidates shared this and were not faulted for it); the morion floats upright rather than upside down; and the body lies in open water by the barrels rather than pressed against the hull planks.

Clean. This is the r3-approved v03 composition with the painted balloon removed. Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, a clean chin with light captivity stubble, a small gold ear stud, long curly hair, the empty hinged collar, a torn ochre tunic and a bandaged hand in an iron manacle, its chain running back to the hidden wrist. The visible arm is his right, so the left forearm stays hidden. He is half out of the timber hatch in driving rain, twisted round to shout down at the backs of the prisoners' heads. The flat-tread ladder matches 7.2 and 7.3, and the glass deck lantern is allowed in a Portuguese setting. There is no text, blood or noose. The rain-streaked sky and rigging above and right of his head (about x 0.57 to 0.88, y 0.02 to 0.24) is low-detail and clear of his face for the balloon. Two notes. (1) A cream frame border with a black keyline is painted round the edges (cream to about x 11 and from x 1524, to y 7 and from y 999, with the keyline just inside). Set visible_rect to about [16, 12, 1520, 993] to crop it out. (2) The blurred background deck figures, a sailor in a wide hat at left-centre and a crewman in a brimmed hat at right, have no readable faces and do not read as a guard confronting him.

v11 is the only candidate offered, and it is acceptable. It is the same staging as the earlier v01 pick, now without painted boxes. It shows the storm on deck: driving rain, a Dutch-angle heel, the snapped mainmast with torn canvas, and the black-and-gold carved stern castle rising aft. The crew are mixed and barefoot, in loose shirts, slops and head cloths, with no uniforms or oilskins. One sailor has a knife in his teeth, men heave at the pump handles, and nobody looks at Nagoji. Nagoji is thrown against the starboard rail, gripping a line, with a half-loose rope coil at his bare feet. He is on-model: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, long curly hair and torn ochre tunic. He wears the empty hinged collar with its ring at the side, and the hobble chain is clear. His brand arm shows no brand. There is no gore and no noose. Both captions can sit in clear stormy sky at top left (x 0.08 to 0.40, y 0 to 0.2) and top right (x 0.85 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.25), away from every face. Costume and setting match the chosen 8.3 (v08). Minor faults, none disqualifying: (1) The wrist chain hangs from the right cuff and never visibly joins the left cuff, because his hands are spread wide. (2) The right wrist may have a doubled cuff. (3) His hands are not bandaged, though the cuffs cover the wrists. (4) A small gilt name board low on the stern gallery (about x 0.87 to 0.92, y 0.33 to 0.36) has letter-like scrollwork up close, but it reads as ornament at print size. A letterer's touch-up there would be harmless. (5) The lower hull of the stern castle meets the sea beyond the curving rail, but it connects to the quarterdeck, so it reads as the same ship.

v02 is the pick. It gives the high angle down the hatch at Keshavrao, and he matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, wide eyes. He wears the iron collar with its side ring, his manacled hands grip the top, and his hobbled bare ankles are chained on a rung below. The painted balloon at top right has no tail, and sky and hatch give room for lettering. Minor points: the shaft is lit warm from below rather than by lightning, and the wrist chain is only visible dangling from one cuff. v01 is the same image without the iron collar, which the script requires, so it is rejected.

v08 is the pick. Nagoji is small in the mid-foreground, seen from behind, braced at the rail. His iron collar has the ring at the side, and his visible right wrist is manacled, chained and bandaged, with the left forearm hidden. A lightning-lit wave rears above the ship. The two insets along the bottom show Keshavrao's manacled hands clamped on the hatch rim with the chain between them, and a shattered spar in the sea. The crew have their backs to him. The painted boxes sit over sky and wave crest, clear of faces. Minor points: the sails look intact, whereas 8.1 has a snapped mainmast. One foreground sailor wears a tricorn and waistcoat, which fits the period but is not the head cloths of 8.1. The spar inset does not show the ship's side. v07 and v06 are the same art without the bandage on his hand. v01 to v05 draw Nagoji large, not small, and show Keshavrao's face in the inset instead of just his hands. In v01 a painted box also covers Keshavrao's eyes.

This is the only candidate, and it is usable. The wave crest breaks over the ship's rail and fills the frame, with no figures, no text and no anachronism. Weak points: the frame is 3:2 rather than a narrow strip, so it needs a horizontal crop through the middle band (rail plus curling water). The rail is a light open balustrade rather than the dark solid bulwark of 8.3. The sky is greyer and lighter than the night storm of 8.1 and 8.3, though it can pass as a lightning flash.

Acceptable, with minor deviations. Keshavrao matches his sheet: short hacked hair, a young face, grey-brown tunic, white dhoti, an empty iron collar with a side ring, manacles, and no ear stud. He is half out of the hatch with his left hand clamped on the rim and his right hand at his side, and the inset of Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hand clawing the rope coil sits in the upper left. There is no painted text, balloon, blood or anachronism. Minor points: (1) His moustache is a little heavier than 'faint', but still thin and nothing like Nagoji's curled one. (2) His hair is spiky and wet, not slicked flat, and the hairline graze is barely visible (only a faint mark at the right temple). (3) The right hand reads more as hanging and bracing than as twitching for a missing sword. (4) The wrist chain runs from his right cuff to the waist and vanishes behind the tunic, so the slack between the wrists is vague. (5) In the inset both cuffs, joined by the chain, can read as sitting on one bandaged forearm. At inset size it passes as the chained pair of wrists, and the clawed hand shows 4 digits (thumb plus 3 fingers), which is plausible for the grip. (6) The deck is rain-slick rather than foam-awash, but the grey-white post-wave light fits 9.2. Lettering space: put the caption in the top band of the inset (about x 0.10-0.30, y 0.01-0.18 of the frame), above the fingers, over the blurred background. Put Keshavrao's balloon in the open rain sky at the upper right (about x 0.56-0.95, y 0.02-0.22), with its tail down-left to his mouth.

Minor issues only. v05 and v06 are the same art; only the size of the painted reserves differs. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, long curly hair, collar with side ring, bandaged manacled wrists, ankle irons with hobble chain, torn ochre tunic. His arms are extended at the end of the throw rather than mid-heave, so it reads a little like holding the rope. The rope lies short, halfway across, with coils on the wet deck and water pouring off at the scuppers on the right. Keshavrao (collar, manacles, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, cream dhoti) is already fully out on the deck in front of a raised hatch coaming. In 9.3 he is back half inside the hatch. Each wrist chain dangles from its own cuff rather than visibly linking the pair, and Nagoji's long ochre tunic hem covers most of the cream dhoti. Hands are sound, and there is no text, gore or anachronism. Lettering: the caption goes in the upper left over the storm sky. Nagoji's balloon fits best in the sky and rigging at top centre, between his head and the mast, with its tail to his mouth. The painted box at the lower right will be covered.

Minor issues only. Keshavrao is half out of the hatch with the rope looped in his manacled hands, and the short wrist chain is caught across the rope. He has the collar with its side ring, faint moustache, short hair and grey-brown tunic, and his hands are sound. The rope runs back across the deck to Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hands at the left edge, and the next wave rears on the right with its white edge curling toward the hatch. Nagoji is cut off at the nose by the top edge, so the ear stud is out of frame. Moustache, light stubble and a clean chin show. His ochre cloth drapes over his forearms like sleeves (this keeps the left forearm covered), and Keshavrao's tunic droops over his left upper arm. There is no text and no noose: the loop is at his chest, not his neck. Rejected: v01 (3:2) and v03 have no collar on Keshavrao. v02 has no collar and paints a panel border inside the image, with dark cloud bands above and below.

Minor issues only. This is a medium shot rather than a true wide. The plunging bow is implied by the grey and white wave filling the background rather than drawn. His shin and raised knee rest over and among the coil rather than pressing squarely on it. Nagoji matches: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, gold ear stud, empty collar with side ring, bandaged manacled hands with the chain sagging between the wrists, and a cream dhoti. The ochre drape covers the far (left) forearm. The rope runs dead straight and taut to the right, into the white water. The two caption reserves sit top-left and top-right, clear of his face and hands. Backup v02 is a truer wide: a sleeveless tunic per the sheet, his dhoti knee on the coil, the ankle cuff with hobble chain, and a better 3:1 aspect. But his left forearm is bare from elbow to cuff (outer side toward camera), so it is weaker on the brand-concealment rule. Rejected: v06 has no collar and the rope wraps a bitt. v07 runs a chain from the collar ring to the manacles, so the collar is not empty. v04 and v05 show hands only, with no knee or coil. v03 has no coil. v01 has a 2:1 frame and is weaker.

Minor issues only. The bandages are stripped into long trailing strips but not visibly scorched, and the palms are only mildly reddened. There is no torn flesh and no blood. Both open palms face the viewer with thumbs to the viewer's right, so the handedness is slightly ambiguous, but it reads naturally at print size. The knee pinning the coil is under the ochre tunic hem here, while in 9.4 v08 the cream dhoti shows at the knee. The staging matches the script. The rope has parted at a frayed end on the coil side of his hands, the free length slides through his open palms toward the rail and the spray at the right, his knee pins the coil, and the manacles are linked by their short chain. The two caption reserves sit top-left over the tunic and top-right over the rain and rigging, clear of the hands. Rejected: v01 to v07 all break the rope between his two hands. v04 to v06 also lack the knee and coil, v07's wrist cuffs are not linked, and v01 and v02 are 3:2.

Minor: the ladder in the hatch reads as intact, not clearly broken, and Nagoji is a medium-size figure rather than 'small' in the frame. Everything else matches: empty hatch with water pouring into the hold, nobody there, empty hinged collar with its ring, wrist chain, hobble chain, reddened open palms trailing bandage strips, and the frayed rope coil at his feet. Face matches the sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud). His left forearm is covered by the tunic sleeve. The top-right painted box sits over sky and rigging. The other candidates fail. v03 is the same art but with the left inner forearm bare and turned to camera, which breaks the hidden-brand rule. v01 and v02 also show the bare left forearm, and they put a loose bandage strip at his feet where the frayed rope coil should be.

v03 is clean. Tight rain-soaked face on the right: thick curled moustache, stubbled clean chin, gold stud, collar with ring, eyes turned right toward the off-panel hatch. On the left a ragged-edged dust memory shows Deccan riders galloping away with backs turned (anonymous), a saffron pennant with no marks, and a fallen comrade face down beside his fallen horse, with no blood. Both painted boxes sit on the memory, clear of the face. Small deviation: the horse lies down instead of standing riderless. Backup v07 has a standing riderless horse but carries painted black letterbox bars top and bottom that must be cropped out, and its riders are small silhouettes. v04, v05 and v06 fail the 'tight on face' framing (seated full figure). v01 and v02 repeat v03's art at 3:2 and would lose the face or the memory in a full-width crop.

v03: profile at the rail, facing out to sea. Two turns of rope round his chest pulled tight by bandaged, manacled hands, frayed free end trailing, empty collar with ring, joined wrist chain, and a ragged tunic flap and bandage over the far (left) forearm. The splintered, barnacled spar rides the foam. The hobble chain is out of frame because of the waist-up crop, and the spar sits mid-distance rather than directly below. There is open storm sky right of his face for the 'Forgive me' balloon. Rejected: v01 (Portuguese guards on deck, not in the beat), v04 (rope tied to the spar and a hauling pose), v05 (hands on the rail, no knotting), v06 (hands behind his back and no collar), v07 (confused staging with no rail between him and the sea).

v07 is the only candidate whose wrists stay joined by the short wrist chain. It also shows the hobble chain at the ankles, the collar, two turns of rope round his chest with the frayed end trailing, both forearms under tunic flap and bandage, lightning sky, black water, and the ship's rail behind him. Face matches (moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). Caveat: he leaps screen-left with the ship on the right, the reverse of 10.3 where he faces screen-right toward the sea. That break in screen direction is acceptable across the cut, but a horizontal flip would restore continuity if the page reads awkwardly (both forearms are covered, so a flip is safe for the brand rule). Rejected: v02 (arms flung wide, only one wrist chained, rope rising from behind his neck), v03, v04 and v05 (arms spread with separate chain stubs on each wrist, implying a broken wrist chain), v01 (guards reaching from the rail, arms spread), v06 (a wrist chain and ankle chain running back to the ship, a gold hoop at the neck).

v04: underwater just below the white foam of his entry, looking up past him. Collar with ring, gold stud, moustache and clean chin match. Joined manacles and fists at the bottom edge, rope knotted round his chest, and the rope's free end snakes up toward the barnacled, splintered spar without being tied to it. The ship's dark hull heels away beyond. Minor: at extreme zoom a few barnacles have hole patterns that faintly suggest faces, but at print size they read as barnacles. Rejected: v01 and v02 (rope lashed around the spar instead of a free end), v03 (collar drawn split in two floating pieces, rope ends on the spar, 3:2 format), v05 (no collar, reddish marks on the shoulders, spar reads as part of the hull).
